claim: A 5 W panel covers the 0.54 Wh daily need on a dull rainy-season day
law: Energy balance: P_panel x peak sun hours x derating >= E_day; at 1 peak sun hour the yield is 3.0 Wh, still above the need
check: in 7.5 Wh/day, out 0.5396 Wh/day

claim: The battery runs the unit for 7 days or more without sun
law: Autonomy = usable energy / daily need, with an 0.85 efficient 3.3 V converter (independent review): 15.36 Wh / 0.635 Wh; 28.5 days without the converter loss
check: 24.2 days >= 7 days

claim: The panel refills an empty battery in 3 clear days or fewer, also on 45 degC days
law: Days = usable energy / (energy the charger may take - daily need); 1.19 days on a mild clear day; on a 45 degC day only 5.8 Wh may be charged under the shield (C4), so it depends on S5 (independent review)
check: 2.94 days <= 3 days

claim: Under the ventilated sun shield the enclosure stays near 51 degC on a 45 degC day and the battery can charge for about 5 h
law: Lumped thermal model: absorbed sun (absorptance 0.70, 900 W/m2 direct) against 10 W/m2K over the exposed area, time constant 13 min; the shield passes a quarter of the solar gain (assumed)
check: Peak 50.8 degC, 5.4 sun hours below the 45 degC charge limit; the shield factor 0.25 is an assumption, to measure at TRL 4

claim: One 90 s flush leaves less than 5 % of the previous hour's water in the cell when the chlorine is read
law: Well-mixed cell: stale fraction = exp(-(Q t - V_tube) / V_cell), Q 0.5 L/min, t 80 s, V_cell 0.185 L

claim: At a 0.5 bar site a 110 s flush leaves less than 5 % stale water
law: As S6 at 0.35 L/min below the regulator's compensating pressure (90 s gives 8.5 %, independent review); 15.4 L/day

claim: Hourly flushing uses 20 L/day or less at the regulator's upper tolerance
law: Volume = 0.55 L/min x 90 s x 24 readings (pressure-compensating regulator, +10 %); ten confirming readings a month add about 0.25 L/day; PR-008 counts the hourly schedule only (WWT-DEC-001 O4, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)
check: 19.8 L/day <= 20 L/day

claim: The open air-break vent at the cell outlet stops the drain hose siphoning the cell and stops drain water reaching the cell
law: A siphon needs a sealed, liquid-filled path; a vent open to the atmosphere above the outlet holds atmospheric pressure there (hydrostatics). An air gap is the highest category of backflow protection in EN 1717 practice
check: The vent rises 60 mm above the outlet and stays open; the inlet side is S30

claim: Cell water cannot flow back into the supply through the inlet when the main goes to negative pressure
law: On an intermittent supply the main can fall below atmospheric pressure and draw water back; one plain check valve is not a verifiable barrier (independent review). The cell is closed and full, so a back-siphon would pull cell water through the inlet
check: Two check valves in series (supply train and cell inlet) and the normally closed latching valve, shut 58 min in each hour (WWT-DEC-001 F8); a verifiable backflow device or an inlet air gap to assess with the operator under the local code (WWT-REG-001 R4)

claim: Bubbles of 100 um and larger clear the 66 mm cavity during the 30 s wait at 5 degC
law: Stokes rise velocity, Re 0.24 (below 1, so Stokes holds), water at 5 degC; the wait clears bubbles of about 78 um and up, not bubbles stuck to the windows

claim: An 860 nm LED with a 90 degree scatter detector and a 180 degree transmitted-light detector measures turbidity from 0 to 100 units
law: ISO 7027-1:2016 gives 860 nm diffuse radiation at 90 degrees for low turbidity (reported in FNU, about 0 to 40) and attenuation of the transmitted beam for higher turbidity (FAU); the cell has both detectors, so the upper range uses the 180 degree reading (independent review: say FNU, not NTU); Kelley et al. (2014) built an open-source turbidimeter on the same principle
check: Principle and wavelength match the standard; accuracy of this cell (R2) to verify with stabilised standards at TRL 4

claim: The 48.3 x 3.2 mm pole carries a 35 m/s gust on the panel, sun shield and pole with a factor of at least 1.5 on yield
law: sigma = M / Z at the footing, M 281 N m, Z 4.80 cm3; S235 yield 235 MPa / 1.5
check: 59 MPa <= 157 MPa

claim: The 300 mm x 600 mm footing resists the gust load with a factor of at least 1.5, also in saturated sand
law: Broms, short rigid free-head pile: H_u = 0.5 gamma D L^3 Kp / (e + L), Kp 3; dry medium sand (18 kN/m3) 890 N, saturated sand (9 kN/m3, independent review) shown; clay and made ground to assess at the survey visit

claim: After 20 % capacity fade from hot-weather ageing the battery still runs 7 days without sun
law: LiFePO4 loses capacity faster when held above 45 degC (independent review); autonomy with 80 % of the capacity and the converter loss
check: 19.4 days >= 7 days

claim: Charging is blocked below 0 degC and above 45 degC, which protects the LiFePO4 cell
law: Lithium plating on charge below 0 degC and faster ageing when charged hot are known for LiFePO4; cell datasheets give a 0 to 45 degC charge window
check: Charger with temperature cut-offs (BOM line 6) and NTC on the cell; to confirm in the charger datasheet (WWT-DEC-001, to confirm 8)

claim: The battery's cell count matches its stated capacity, 6 Ah at 3.2 V (19.2 Wh)
law: Pack capacity = cells in parallel x cell capacity; one 32700 LiFePO4 cell is 6.0 Ah (reseller listing; maker datasheet to obtain, WWT-DEC-001 to confirm 9); mismatch between stated and built capacity

claim: At pH 8 and 25 degC about a quarter of free chlorine is hypochlorous acid
law: HOCl fraction = 1 / (1 + 10^(pH - pKa)), pKa from Morris (1966): 3000 / T - 10.0686 + 0.0253 T
check: 0.004 absolute error vs 0.26 <= 0.02 absolute error vs 0.26

claim: A membrane-free graphite three-electrode sensor reads free chlorine from 0 to 2 mg/L with drift below 0.15 mg/L per month
law: Amperometric reduction of HOCl at a carbon working electrode (Pan et al. 2015; pencil graphite electrodes, PLOS ONE 2021); long-term field drift of low-cost sensors is reported in Water Science and Technology (2025), not checked in full
check: Response within known science; the drift that R1 and R10 allow (about 0.15 mg/L per month with the shared photometer, WWT-CAL-001 E12; 0.13 before the decisions of 2026-10-25) is unverified

claim: The chlorine error budget meets the PR-001 target at 0.5 mg/L and pH 7.5 before drift
law: Root sum of squares of the DPD reference 0.07 mg/L, pH change between visits on the HOCl fraction and temperature residual, with the stale-water bias added linearly (independent review); the HOCl fraction is corrected for the measured temperature through pKa(T)

claim: The chlorine error budget meets the PR-001 target at 1.5 mg/L at every pH
law: Corrected budget as S13 (independent review): at 1.5 mg/L the pH terms dominate; a one-point calibration at 0.5 mg/L carries the reference error as a relative error at 1.5 mg/L. PR-001 restated by Amish on 2026-10-25 as +/-30 % above 1.0 mg/L (WWT-DEC-001 O5), with the shared DPD photometer (+/-0.03 mg/L +/-3 %) as the monthly reference (O2)
check: 8 of 8 cases met calibrated at the reading level; worst FC 1.5 mg/L pH 8.5: +/-0.392 against +/-0.450 mg/L; with the photometer and calibrated at 0.5 mg/L where worse, 8 of 8 (WWT-CAL-001 E12; worst +/-0.411 against +/-0.450 mg/L)
closed_by: WWT-DEC-001 O2 and O5 (decided by Amish 2026-10-25); WWT-CAL-001 E11, E12

claim: The membrane-free sensor's current does not depend on the flow past it
law: Amperometric currents depend on mass transport, so on flow; the pressure-compensating regulator holds the flow above 0.7 bar, but at 0.5 bar it is 30 % lower (independent review)
check: Flow dependence of this sensor unknown; read at the end of the flush at a held flow; to measure at TRL 4

claim: The three-electrode sensor works in low-conductivity water
law: Below about 50 uS/cm the solution resistance between the electrodes grows and the potentiostat loses control (independent review)
check: Conductivity of candidate sources to survey; a conductivity floor to set at TRL 4

claim: A silver/silver chloride pseudo-reference stays stable in low-chloride drinking water
law: The Ag/AgCl potential follows the chloride activity (Nernst); without a filled reference chamber it moves with the water's chloride
check: Potentiostat holds the working electrode against it; drift of the reference adds to S12; to measure at TRL 4

claim: Flushed water (18 L/day at up to 2 mg/L free chlorine) to the tapstand basin is environmentally negligible
law: Mass balance: 36 mg of chlorine a day (40 mg at the regulator tolerance), the same water the tap already delivers to the basin; option A adds no reagent, unlike option B, whose drain must go to a soakaway (B5)
check: Same water as the tap; no reagent added

claim: PVC, ASA, EPDM, polycarbonate and stainless parts withstand 0.2 to 2 mg/L free chlorine and outdoor sun
law: These materials are used in chlorinated water and outdoors at these levels; ASA and polycarbonate are UV-stabilised grades; EPDM is preferred over nitrile in chlorinated water
check: Wetted parts drain to waste behind a check valve, so taste and leaching do not reach users; grades to confirm

claim: A monthly wipe keeps the cell windows and the chlorine electrode clean enough
law: Biofilm and particle fouling of optical windows and electrodes in drinking water grows over weeks; residual chlorine slows it
check: Rate at a turbid site unknown; to observe at TRL 4 and in field trials

claim: Alert thresholds of 0.2 mg/L free chlorine and 5 NTU match field guidance for the point of delivery
law: WHO guidance as summarised for field use: at least 0.2 mg/L free chlorine at the point of delivery; chlorination loses effect as turbidity rises, markedly above about 10 NTU, so the 5 NTU alert is the earlier warning; the device reports measurements only (PR-013)
check: Defaults decided by Amish (WWT-DDR-001 D6); at 0.2 mg/L the budget is about +/-0.08 mg/L, so a reading of 0.2 means about 0.12 to 0.28 (WWT-CAL-001 E3)

claim: Calibration chemicals are handled safely by a caretaker
law: DPD is harmful if swallowed and can sensitise skin, so tablets are handled with gloves and tested water goes to the drain, not back to a container; formazin is made from toxic precursors (hydrazine sulfate, hexamethylenetetramine), so only prepared, stabilised standards are used
check: Rule in WWT-PRC-001 Safety and the build plan; disposal with the operator

claim: The enclosure (1.17 to 1.43 m) and the cell (0.81 to 0.90 m) sit within standing working reach; the panel is cleaned from the ground
law: Comfortable standing work and reach heights for adults lie about 0.8 to 1.5 m (anthropometric tables, Pheasant and Haslegrave, Bodyspace); the panel at 2.16 m is out of reach for small adults (independent review), so it is wiped with a long-handled brush
check: Heights from the model; the 30 min monthly visit is a task analysis (WWT-CAL-001 J3)

claim: The water-filled cell survives a 0 degC night
law: At 0 degC air a small exposed volume can fall below freezing by night-sky radiation, and ice expands about 9 % (independent review)
check: Freezing margin not shown; at sites near 0 degC drain the cell for the cold season or insulate it; to assess with the partner

claim: The temperature probe reads the water to +/-0.5 degC
law: The DS18B20 is +/-0.5 degC; it is read after a flush of four cell volumes of supply water, but the black cell heats in the sun between flushes (independent review)
check: Sun-heating bias of the reading to measure at TRL 4

claim: Closing the valve at 4 bar does not overstress the sample line
law: Joukowsky surge dp = rho a v, tube velocity 0.57 m/s, wave speed about 350 m/s in small PE tube (estimate): 2.0 bar on top of 4 bar, against about 10 bar for 1/4 in PE tube (typical rating, BOM line 14)
check: 6 bar <= 10 bar

claim: The hot-day enclosure simulation uses a stable, converged time step
law: Explicit Euler is stable and within about 4 % of the exact first-order response for dt / tau below 0.1 (dt 60 s)
check: 0.075 dt / tau <= 0.1 dt / tau

claim: One LTE-M upload, network attach included, costs about 20 mWh
law: SIM7000-class modem: about 150 mA at 3.8 V for the same 140 s per attach and post that S21 assumes (independent review)
check: claimed 20 mWh, estimate 22.2 mWh (ratio 0.90)

claim: Uploads stay under 1 MB a month
law: Six sessions a day of 780 B payload; with TLS session resumption about 1.2 kB overhead; a full handshake every session (about 6 kB) would give 1.22 MB (independent review), so the firmware keeps sessions
check: 0.36 MB/month <= 1 MB/month

claim: An SMS leaves within 15 min of a confirmed crossing, with three tries
law: Attach 120 s and send 20 s per try, 3 min between tries; the firmware bounds each try at 140 s; from the event itself, with retries, up to 92 min (H4)
check: 13 min <= 15 min

claim: The latching valve opens at every supply pressure from 0.5 to 4 bar
law: A direct-acting solenoid valve needs no minimum pressure difference (a pilot-operated valve needs about 0.2 to 0.5 bar), but a small direct-acting valve has a maximum opening differential (independent review)
check: BOM line 13 specifies direct acting and rated to open against at least 4 bar; to confirm in the datasheet

claim: DPD colorimetry reads free chlorine from 0 to 2 mg/L in a 12 mm cuvette
law: DPD reacts with free chlorine to a magenta colour read near 515 nm (ISO 7393-2; EPA 330.5 adaptations in commercial photometers)
check: Standard method; used by field photometers and online analysers

claim: DPD and buffer reagents keep their strength for a month at up to 50 degC in the cabinet
law: Liquid DPD indicator oxidises and darkens with heat and air; suppliers give shelf lives at room temperature
check: Shelf life at 50 degC unknown; to assess with a supplier

claim: 80 mL of each reagent lasts 90 days at 0.03 mL per test and 24 tests a day
law: Mass balance of reagent
check: in 80 mL, out 64.8 mL

claim: The analyser needs about 0.8 Wh/day, within the 5 W panel
law: Option A's budget plus two 0.5 W pumps for 5 s and a 0.3 W stirrer for 30 s per test
check: claimed 0.8 Wh/day, estimate 0.68 Wh/day (ratio 1.18)

claim: Reacted sample with DPD and phosphate buffer can go to a soakaway
law: About 1.5 mL of reagent a day in 18 L of water; DPD (N,N-diethyl-p-phenylenediamine) is harmful if swallowed, so the drain must not reach the basin users fill from
check: Drain to a soakaway, not the basin; to assess with the operator

claim: The same 860 nm LED and 90 degree detector read turbidity in the cuvette before the reagent goes in
law: Nephelometry as S10
check: Same principle as option A

claim: ORP and pH electrodes estimate free chlorine within the R1 target
law: ORP follows the log of the HOCl activity and the pH, and other redox couples move it; it is used as a control signal, and tracks chlorine only loosely in the 0.2 to 2 mg/L range
check: Principle known; meeting +/-0.2 mg/L unlikely without frequent calibration

claim: A 12 mm probe in a compression gland holds against 4 bar
law: Push-out force = p x pi d^2 / 4 at 4 bar; small PVC compression glands hold well over 100 N (to confirm in the gland datasheet)

claim: Probes in the riser read the water people draw, without flushing
law: While the tap runs, the riser carries the supply water; between draws the water stands in the pipe and the reading is of stale water
check: Readings valid only during draws (a paddle flow switch wakes the unit); no reading at night when nobody draws

claim: Insertion turbidity in the running pipe is not upset by bubbles and daylight
law: Entrained air from a tap opening scatters light like particles; the opaque manifold keeps daylight out
check: Bubble bias in flowing water unknown; to assess

claim: With no valve and no flush the manifold needs about 0.4 Wh/day
law: Uploads, sleep and status light as option A, plus 24 wake-ups of 20 s at 0.264 W
check: claimed 0.4 Wh/day, estimate 0.242 Wh/day (ratio 1.65)

claim: Cutting the riser and fitting two unions keeps the tapstand watertight and serviceable
law: Threaded unions on 25 mm galvanised pipe are standard plumbing; it changes the tapstand, which the problem statement rules out
check: Within known science; conflicts with the PRB constraint of one tee only
